header: ROAD-8: racing-line kerbs at named Nordschleife corners (docs/road-0068-0069-analysis.md section 5.3: kerbs only at selected corners and runoff edges, never a blanket perimeter). Read by WorldRoadProfile.read_kerbs; every entry names a LOOP segment of data/regions/eifel_ring/skeleton.json (loops[0].segments, whose order is the travel order: all 92 chain head to tail, so a segment's point order is the travel direction).

side is in road-travel direction: left / right / both. chainage_from and chainage_to are metres along that segment, the same chainage WorldRoadProfile._nearest_chord returns and RoadBuilder.Strip.chainages carries. The kerb replaces the plain ROAD-5 lip on that side inside the window, faded in and out over KERB_FADE_M of chainage so the window's ends are steps in nothing.

SELECTION RULE (authored): a kerb only at a segment whose skeleton.json name is a documented corner (docs/nordschleife-data-sources.md section 4: T-numbers plus named sections), never the generic 'Nuerburgring Nordschleife' name and never a plain straight. The corner's inside is read from the loop's own geometry: the signed heading change over the segment's points in the x-east / z-south frame, positive to the right of travel. 'raised' (the red/white toothed apex kerb, WorldRoadProfile.KERB_RAISED_HEIGHT_M) goes on the inside edge of the named tight corners; 'flat' (the painted 0.02 m band, KERB_FLAT_HEIGHT_M over KERB_FLAT_WIDTH_M) at fast-corner entries and exits and on outside edges where the runoff is documented as limited (data-sources section 4: 'Armco steel guardrails run close to the road; runoff is limited to gravel or grass in most places') and a raised kerb would trip a fast car.

EXCLUDED on purpose: 414785755-0 Karussell (its bank is its own mechanism, KARUSSELL_BANK); 683303211-0 Doettinger Hoehe and the certified ring-drive stretch (tests/ring_drive_test.gd: 2000 m from that segment's chainage 30, through the three unnamed straights and Antoniusbuche) and the frozen offroad/marks tests' straight; Tiergarten, Hohenrain, T13 and Sabine-Schmitz-Kurve, the segments right after that stretch, for margin. Hatzenbogen 1009142895-0 is wanted (the driver's own ask): its first raised window starts at chainage 100 because tests/road_edge_test.gd pins the plain lip at the issue-0068 pose's right wheels, chainage 82 of that segment.

GRIP: the existing shoulder classification answers - a wheel outside pavement inside a kerb window is what Surfaces.classify names it today (the 1.5 m shoulder rule: gravel). The kerb is a height feature the suspension reads, as ROAD-5's lip is; a named kerb surface class is a follow-up needing a freeze ruling on surfaces.json / surfaces.gd.

TELEMETRY: the driver's own free laps of 2026-09-28 (sessions 0190_153507_free.jsonl and 0192_172931_free.jsonl, read only) were joined to the loop by the same chord geometry; where an entry cites a session the driver's line ran within 1.2 m inside to 1.5 m outside of that edge in that chainage window. Where telemetry was silent or ambiguous the window is authored from the geometry and the docs alone, and the basis says so.

kerbs.basis: Hatzenbogen (skeleton.json name), a right-hander of +89 degrees over 468 m; its first arc turns +30 degrees between chainage 98 and 175, the inside edge is the right. The driver asked for a kerb here. Starts at 100, past the issue-0068 pose's right wheels at chainage 82 whose plain lip tests/road_edge_test.gd pins. Session 0190 clipped this inside edge at chainage 9-14 (the entry) and ran 147 samples off the left: the corner is driven on the racing line.

Hatzenbogen's outside edge between its two right-hand arcs (chainage 175-276 turns under 8 degrees): where a car that runs wide out of the first arc lands. Session 0190 has 147 samples off the left edge of this segment, session 0192 none. A flat painted band, the outside rule (data-sources section 4: limited runoff, barriers close), never a raised kerb on the outside of a fast arc.

Hatzenbogen's second arc: +50 degrees between chainage 276 and 361, the tighter of the two, the inside edge the right. Authored from the geometry; the telemetry sessions did not clip this apex within 1.2 m.

Hocheichen (skeleton.json name), the right-hander: +60 degrees over the segment, all of it between chainage 131 and 204. Sessions 0190 (chainage 151-172, 67 samples) and 0192 (153-194, 113 samples) clipped this inside edge.

Hocheichen's left-hand exit (skeleton.json name, the -1 segment): -28 degrees between chainage 14 and 38, the inside edge the left. Sessions 0190 (chainage 5-13, 59 samples) and 0192 (0-27, 62 samples) clipped it.

Flugplatz (skeleton.json name), the fast right-hand crest: +36 degrees between chainage 32 and 80, taken near flat out, so a painted flat band and not a raised kerb on the inside. Session 0190 clipped this edge at chainage 53-80 (86 samples), session 0192 at 53-62.
Flugplatz's second right kink: +28 degrees between chainage 161 and 201, fast, the inside edge the right; flat for the same reason as the first. Session 0192 clipped it at chainage 174-184.

Schwedenkreuz (skeleton.json name), the fastest left of the lap: -30 degrees spread over chainage 250-393, the inside edge the left. A raised kerb at this speed would trip the car: flat. Session 0192 clipped the edge at chainage 378-384; otherwise authored from the geometry.

Aremberg (skeleton.json name), the tight right-hander after Schwedenkreuz: +133 degrees between chainage 13 and 162, the inside edge the right. Authored from the geometry; neither session clipped this inside edge within 1.2 m (both stayed between -2.2 and +2.5 m of the centre).

Aremberg's outside edge through the apex and the exit: the barrier side of a tight corner (data-sources section 4: guardrails close, runoff limited). A painted flat band on the outside, per the outside rule. Authored from the geometry and the docs.

Adenauer Forst (skeleton.json name), the chicane's tight left: -108 degrees between chainage 196 and 285 (the two -15.5 degree kinks at 256 and 264 are the apex), the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions clipped the right edge (the following right) and not this one.

Adenauer Forst's tight right out of the chicane: +91 degrees between chainage 303 and 361, the inside edge the right. Session 0192 clipped this inside edge at chainage 319-350 (106 samples), session 0190 at 363-367.

Metzgesfeld (skeleton.json name, the -1 segment), the long left: -50 degrees between chainage 148 and 253, the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions ran off the right (the outside) here, not the inside.

Kallenhard (skeleton.json name), its entry: a -70 degree left between chainage 6 and 74 whose OUTSIDE is the right edge. Session 0190 ran that outside edge at chainage 34-56 (145 samples within 1.2 m in to 1.5 m out): a runoff edge, so a flat painted band under the outside rule (data-sources section 4).
Kallenhard proper, the right-hander: +130 degrees between chainage 272 and 379, the inside edge the right. Authored from the geometry; the sessions did not clip this apex within 1.2 m.

Wehrseifen (skeleton.json name), the tight left: -150 degrees between chainage 180 and 253, the inside edge the left. Sessions 0190 (chainage 158-182 and 227-241) and 0192 (155-172) clipped this inside edge.
Wehrseifen's exit right towards Breidscheid: +55 degrees between chainage 273 and 338, the inside edge the right. Authored from the geometry.

Breidscheid (skeleton.json name, the 683061814-1 segment), the left-hander before the bridge: -75 degrees between chainage 24 and 88, the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions kept to the platform here.

Bergwerk (skeleton.json name), the right-hander: +119 degrees over the segment, its tightest 65 degrees between chainage 70 and 134, the inside edge the right. Authored from the geometry; session 0192 clipped the inside edge only at the exit (chainage 398-404).

Steilstrecke (skeleton.json name, the -1 segment), the climbing right before the Karussell: +118 degrees between chainage 5 and 117, the inside edge the right. Sessions 0190 (chainage 63-98, 102 samples) and 0192 (1-15 and 85-107) clipped this inside edge. The Karussell itself, 414785755-0, carries no kerb.

Bruennchen (skeleton.json name Brünnchen, the -1 segment), the second right-hander: +96 degrees between chainage 46 and 147, the inside edge the right. Session 0192 clipped this inside edge at chainage 62-108 (125 samples).
Eiskurve (skeleton.json name), the left-hander: -82 degrees between chainage 50 and 124, the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions kept to the platform here.

Mini-Karussell (skeleton.json name), the banked left: -110 degrees between chainage 138 and 219, the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions kept to the platform here. Not the Karussell: this segment carries no bank label, so the kerb is a plain edge feature on it.

Schwalbenschwanz (skeleton.json name, the -2 segment), the tight left of the swallowtail: -60 degrees between chainage 12 and 83, the inside edge the left. Authored from the geometry; the sessions kept to the platform here.

Galgenkopf (skeleton.json name), the long fast right onto Doettinger Hoehe: +131 degrees spread over 380 m, taken fast, so a painted flat band on the inside and not a raised kerb. Session 0190 clipped this inside edge at chainage 394-469 (153 samples). Ends at 470, well short of the segment's 683 m and of 683303211-0.
